title: Solar is mainstream power | Wood Mackenzie
gist: Energy Gang podcast notes from RE+ 2026: Nextpower president Howard Wenger argues solar plus storage, combined with gas, is key to fast behind-the-meter power for AI data centers, as Nextpower raises its 2030 revenue target from $5.2bn to $7.5bn; he says tax credits remain necessary while tariffs burden solar and storage. The page is a short episode summary with sponsor copy.

themes.theme: AI data centers and behind-the-meter power

insights.claim: AI data-center buildout is pushing US electricity demand up faster than utilities can deliver grid connections, creating demand for behind-the-meter power as an interim solution until grid interconnection is secured.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Grid interconnection delays are a structural tailwind for on-site generation and storage suppliers serving data centers.

themes.theme: Tax credits, tariffs and policy after the midterms

insights.claim: Democratic gains in the 2026 US midterm elections have raised speculation about possible extensions or expansions of renewable energy tax credits, though not everyone in the solar industry is enthusiastic about that prospect.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Policy optionality on clean-energy credits is back in play; renewables equities may re-rate on any credit-extension headlines.
insights.locator: The discussion also goes into the impact

insights.claim: Howard Wenger says Nextpower could thrive without clean-energy incentives on a level playing field with fossil fuels, but that import tariffs and other added costs on solar and storage mean continued tax-credit support is still needed.
insights.speaker: Ed Crooks
insights.so_what: Tariff costs remain the key policy variable for US solar economics; credit rollbacks without tariff relief would hurt project margins.
